content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?Ed Piotrowski WPDE's PostEd Piotrowski WPDE Verified accountMarch 30 at 6:10 PM · Shared with PublicARTEMIS II SCHEDULED TO LAUNCH WEDNESDAYNASA is preparing for a historic return to deep space as the Artemis II mission targets a Wednesday launch, marking the first time humans will travel toward the Moon in more than 50 years. Liftoff is scheduled for 6:24 PM from Kennedy Space Center aboard the powerful Space Launch System rocket, with a two-hour launch window extending until 8:24 PM. At this time, visibility of the rocket from the Carolinas looks unlikely for an on-time launch. Sunset isn’t until 7:35 PM, so skies will still be too bright to see the exhaust plume. However, if the launch is delayed until around 7:50 PM or later, viewing conditions would improve and the plume could become visible 3-5 minutes after liftoff. Space weather forecasters say there’s an 80% chance of favorable launch conditions.The mission will carry four astronauts, Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, on a roughly 10-day journey around the Moon and back. It will be the first crewed flight of NASA’s Orion spacecraft and humanity’s first trip beyond low-Earth orbit since the Apollo era ended in 1972. Rather than landing, Artemis II will follow a “free-return” trajectory, looping around the Moon before heading back to Earth.I’ll keep you updated if anything changes.Ed Piotrowski WPDENews personalitySend messageAll reactions:1.3K142 comments329 sharesLikeCommentMost relevant AuthorEd Piotrowski WPDEVerified account exicting toe see humans going back to the moon!2w37View all 7 repliesLynn WheelerGuess where I am?
